802.title: URL shortener
802.description: Turn long URLs into 7-character codes and redirect at 100× the write rate. The interesting parts are code generation without collisions and a read path that the cache, not the database, carries.

803.title: Pastebin
803.description: Store text snippets and serve them by ID. It looks like the URL shortener, but the payload is 20× bigger, so the real design question is where the bytes live: metadata in a database, content in an object store, hot pastes in a cache.

804.title: Rate limiter
804.description: Protect an API from overload and abuse by rejecting excess requests early with 429. The design choices are the algorithm, where the counters live, and what happens when the limiter itself is slow or down.

805.title: Key-value store
805.description: Design a Dynamo-style store: partition keys over a consistent-hash ring, replicate each key N times and let R and W quorums trade consistency for latency and availability.

806.title: Distributed cache
806.description: Design a Memcached/Redis-style cache tier that absorbs most reads for a database. The hard parts are not the hash map: they are partitioning, hot keys, invalidation races and what happens when a cache node restarts empty.

807.title: News feed
807.description: Show each user a feed of recent posts from the people they follow. The central decision is when to do the work: at write time (fan-out on write, cheap reads) or at read time (fan-out on read, cheap writes).

808.title: Chat (WhatsApp / Messenger)
808.description: One-to-one and group messaging with delivery receipts. The core problems are keeping millions of connections open, storing messages once even when clients retry, and delivering them in order to devices that come and go.

809.title: Notification system
809.description: Accept notification requests from many internal services and deliver them through push, SMS and email providers. The design is a durable queue between fast producers and slow, flaky third parties, with retries, rate limits and user preferences in between.

810.title: Twitter home timeline
810.description: Serve home timelines at hundreds of thousands of reads per second. Twitter's answer was fan-out on write into in-memory timelines, with celebrities merged in at read time — a hybrid that bounds both read cost and write amplification.

811.title: Instagram (photo sharing)
811.description: Upload photos, store them durably and serve them to a global audience. Most bytes never touch your servers: the CDN serves views, an object store keeps the originals, and asynchronous workers produce the sizes clients ask for.

812.title: YouTube (video streaming)
812.description: Accept uploads, transcode them into an adaptive bitrate ladder and stream segments to millions of concurrent viewers. Bandwidth, not requests, is the constraint: the CDN carries the bytes, and transcoding is a large batch pipeline.

813.title: Client
813.description: Generates the scenario's traffic and sends it to one entry point.

814.title: Load balancer
814.description: Spreads requests across the services it can call; health-checks them.

815.title: Service
815.description: Runs your route program for each endpoint.

816.title: Cache
816.description: Fast key-value store with limited memory and eviction.

817.title: Database
817.description: Source of truth. Replicas, replication lag, failover.

818.title: Rate limiter
818.description: Admits up to a rate, rejects the excess with 429.

819.title: DNS
819.description: Resolves a name to its primary record, failing over to the next.

820.title: CDN
820.description: Edge cache per region; misses go to its single origin.

821.title: API gateway
821.description: Auth latency and request-size limits, then passes requests on.

823.title: Queue
823.description: Accepts messages now; workers process them later.

824.title: Worker
824.description: Consumes a queue and runs a route per message.

825.title: Object store
825.description: Durable, slow, priced per request and per GB.

826.title: Search index
826.description: Eventually consistent copy of a source store.

827.title: Dedup store
827.description: Remembers idempotency keys so retries apply once.

828.title: Autoscaler
828.description: Adds or removes workers on its targets (not in the request path).

829.title: Circuit breaker
829.description: Fails fast with 503 while its downstream keeps failing.
